data.gender_notes: Briant is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'bryht', meaning 'bright' or 'shining'. The name Briant has been used in English literature since the Middle Ages, with notable figures such as Sir Briant of Monmouth and Briant the Miller in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales. The name Briant carries the meaning “Bright, shining” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Briant usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.
